title: Automated attenuation + rollback for verified performance profile regressions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We lack an automated, operationally-safe mechanism to reduce traffic to a newly published Redwood-verified performance profile when production telemetry indicates latency/throughput/cost regressions. Currently rollbacks are manual and slow, increasing customer risk and operational toil.

Goal: Ship an attenuation + rollback orchestration that (1) continuously monitors live telemetry against a profile's verified signature, (2) triggers progressive traffic attenuation (e.g., 50% -> 10% -> 0%) when regressions exceed thresholds, and (3) optionally auto-rolls a profile back to the previous pinned version after a confirmatory check. The flow must be auditable, reversible, and surface actionable signals to SRE/PM/Model Stewards.

Scope:
- Implement attenuation policy object and API hooks in publish pipeline and console (configurable per-profile).
- Integrate with runtime telemetry (latency P50/P95, throughput saturation, token-cost deltas) and the profile health scoring engine.
- Add a canary confirmation gate using sampled shadow traffic (5-10%) before final rollback.
- Expose attenuation progress and rationale in the Console UI and in audit logs.

Out of scope for this ticket: cross-region automatic failover, dedicated-only capacity adjustments (follow-up).
success_metrics: Mean time to mitigation < 5 minutes after detected regression
95% of regressions attenuated without manual intervention
Zero customer-facing errors caused by attenuation logic
acceptance_criteria: Policy object created and persisted in profile registry
Console shows attenuation state and audit trail for 3 sample profiles
E2E test: simulate a 30% p95 latency regression -> system reduces traffic to 10% within configured window and produces an incident log
Github PRs merged for runtime hooks and publish pipeline (links in comments)
risks: Edge cases where attenuation confuses downstream billing/cost attribution
Complexity in coordinating attenuation across multi-variant profile publishes
notes: We prefer attenuation thresholds expressed as absolute and relative deltas (e.g., p95 > baseline + 25ms and p95 increase > 10%). The policy should be templatable and tied to a profile's verification signature so it can be enforced or overridden by enterprise tenants.
